title: Targeting peripheral 5-HT2AR enhances antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no PMCID, no full text); Europe PMC datalinks endpoint, which returns only 51 RRIDs (antibody and Jackson mouse-strain catalogue identifiers) plus a Mouse Genome Informatics reference page; NCBI elink from PubMed 42551424 to GEO DataSets, SRA, BioProject and BioSample (all empty); GEO keyword searches (HTR2A + colorectal, enteric glia + colorectal, '8110') returned only unrelated 2024 studies; Zenodo DOI search returned 0 records; the Cell full-text page returns HTTP 403, so nothing could be opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology comes from the abstract only (lysergic acid diethylamide, i.e. LSD, and the new non-brain-penetrant agonist IHCH-8110 act on serotonin receptor 5-HT2AR on enteric glial cells, inducing the signalling proteins CXCL10 and interleukin-18 to recruit CD8+ T cells). A web-search snippet of the Cell full-text page shows the data availability statement as 'Any additional information required to reanalyze the data reported in this paper is available from the lead contact upon request' — I could not open that page to confirm it verbatim, and no accession number was visible anywhere.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable data found anywhere. Paper is subscription-only with no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports no supplementary files, NCBI links to GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample are all empty, Zenodo/Dryad have nothing on the DOI, and the only machine-readable links are antibody/mouse-strain catalogue numbers (RRIDs). The visible data availability wording is 'available from the lead contact upon request' — an explicit A1 failure.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable: no file exists to hold a label column. Any outcome (tumour weight, CD8+ T cell fraction) would have to be read off figures.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs available; mouse treatment groups and flow-cytometry readouts exist only inside figures of a paywalled article.

a5_enough_rows.note: Even if source data were released, this is a mechanistic mouse pharmacology study: cohorts of roughly 5-10 animals per arm, i.e. tens to low hundreds of rows, far under the ~1,500 needed.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <0.1 GB if any source-data tables were ever released
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is the one thing that would not be a problem; everything else is.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no API record of a dataset and no download.

a8_label_provenance.note: Readouts described in the abstract are real physical measurements (tumour growth, immune cell counts), not another model's output — but they are not obtainable.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: there is no accessible dataset attached to this paper, only a paywalled narrative and antibody catalogue numbers.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a drug's chemical structure to predict whether it activates the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor without entering the brain.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need many compound structures paired with both receptor-activation potency and brain-penetration measurements; this paper supplies only one such compound (IHCH-8110) and no table, so the usable example count here is effectively zero.
plain_idea.predict: Two outputs per molecule: potency at the serotonin receptor 5-HT2AR (from cell-based signalling assays) and whether it crosses from blood into the brain (from measured brain-to-plasma concentration ratios in mice).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists making 'non-hallucinogenic psychedelics' would use it to triage compounds before synthesis; but the labelled data for that task lives in ChEMBL and pharmacokinetics datasets, not in this paper.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The interesting adjacent task — predicting serotonin 5-HT2A receptor agonist potency plus blood-brain-barrier penetration from structure, so you can design peripherally restricted agonists — would have to be built from ChEMBL bioactivities and public blood-brain-barrier permeability sets, using a molecule backbone such as ChemBERTa. This paper contributes one compound and no data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no dataset exists to load, so no compute figures are meaningful.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a repository accession (GEO, SRA, Genome Sequence Archive, Zenodo) linked to PubMed 42551424 — there is none, and the article's data statement says 'upon request'. That check took ten minutes and killed it.

verdict_reason: No downloadable data: paywalled, no supplement, no repository deposit, 'available on request'.
